quest.title: Moment of Awakening
quest.description: To get the Jade of Return, you chase the evil dragon all the way to the very end...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x250, Primogem x30, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x3

chapter.num: Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm: Act III
chapter.title: The Tonatiuh Quivers

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Finally! We've got you this time!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, evil dragon, you've pushed your luck twice already, but the third time's not the charm! Now, give us back our stuff!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Or else we'll show you no mercy!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And don't even think about stalling for time!

dialogues.speaker: Cocouik
dialogues.text: Chee... Kuchee!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, that's right... Uh, what was that, Coco?

dialogues.speaker: Cocouik
dialogues.text: ...Travelers from afar, thank you for bringing me here...

dialogues.speaker: Cocouik
dialogues.text: O lost king... The cruel night is about to pass, and the Chosen of Dragons will bring forth the dawn. Now, arise — awaken from your nightmare...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Huh? {NICKNAME}, who are you talking to?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Cocouik, is that you speaking?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Huh? Coco's been making these funny noises, but Paimon can't make out what it's saying... {NICKNAME}, did you hear something?

dialogues.speaker: Cocouik
dialogues.text: My name... is Och-Kan... Once-ruler of Natlan, whose mind was infused into this city...

dialogues.speaker: Cocouik
dialogues.text: When Ochkanatlan's end came, I swallowed the bitter fruit of deadly poison... The poison devoured my soul, transforming it into a dragon furious and fell...

dialogues.speaker: Cocouik
dialogues.text: My end is near. I have finally found the chance... save... my soul...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you going to do?

dialogues.speaker: Cocouik
dialogues.text: The poison... I shall purge it all... And then... you will...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! What are you doing, Coco!? Don't go there!
Finally, after all these years — I have awakened...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?! Who are you? How did you gain the ability to speak?
#What a long journey it has been. {NICKNAME}, Paimon... It is a pleasure to meet you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so you still recognize us! Great! So who are you now, then? Can Paimon still call you Cocouik?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're Och-Kan, then?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Do you mean the Python King — the same one who used to rule all Ochkanatlan?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But didn't Cocouik turn into that? And it still recognizes us — wait, doesn't this mean that this is Cocouik's true...

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: Coco... Yes. That's what that girl called me — the one who woke me up from the Core of Chu'ulel... But I could not save her...

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: Hundreds of years have passed since then... and at last, I've finally found my old body.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Cocouik"...
Cocouik... Yes. Yes. That's what that girl called me — the one who woke me up from the Core of Chu'ulel... But I could not save her...
Hundreds of years have passed since then... and at last, I've finally found my old body.

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: Just call me Och-Kan, please.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Err, are you saying that you're the same Python King who used to rule all Ochkanatlan? But Cocouik turned into you... So all along, it was—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, do you mean that Bona awakened you hundreds of years ago?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That... can't be! We just came on an adventure here with her. She couldn't have been alive for so long, could she?

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: Truly? I could be mistaken... My present memories are as numerous as they are a mess, and I fear I remember things from before far better than my adventures as Cocouik...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Can we still count on you as a comrade, then?

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: Certainly! That is, if you'd still have me... I once split my mind off to protect the people of Ochkanatlan...

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: I never expected my spirit and body to both be swallowed up by the Abyss... To be used by "that person" to commit such an awful litany of crimes...

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: Though my sins cannot be washed away like this Abyssal filth can, this nightmare has finally come to an end — thanks to you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You won't oppose us, will you?

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: Surely not! That is, if you would still accept me... I once split my mind off to protect the people of Ochkanatlan...

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: I never expected my spirit and body to both be swallowed up by the Abyss... To be used by "that person" to commit such an awful litany of crimes...

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: Though my sins cannot be washed away like this Abyssal filth can, this nightmare has finally come to an end — thanks to you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Who's this "person" you're mentioning? Bona mentioned that earlier while we were on the Tonatiuh too. Is there someone pulling the strings behind the scenes whom we don't know about?

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: Heh. Since you're here, you must've already met "that person." You did obtain this... Golden Entreaty, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Golden Treaty," you say... Do you mean this Jade of Return?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, now that you say so, we only got here because that wicked dragon stole it... Hang on, guess we shouldn't call it "wicked" from now on, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I doubt it cares what you call it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, out with it, wicked dragon. Why'd you steal our token?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? Seriously, you're so rude!

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: That Golden Entreaty... is very important.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah. Didn't Bona tell us that it's some kind of key for taming the Abyss?

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: The child is right: It can indeed tame the filth of the Abyss for all of Natlan... But not in the way that you imagine... Which is why I had to hide it on the ship...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What do you mean? That sounds kinda dangerous. Definitely not the sort of thing you'd use willy-nilly... Err, what should we do next, then?

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: Hmm. And another thing. Your companion there, that little Tepetlisaurus...

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: #Yes. {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}... is most similar to me...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What do you mean? You look very different...

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: Our bloodlines have both inherited the Flamelord's Blessing... It is both a gift and a curse. Only by finding another Golden Entreaty and taking them to the volcano, can the Blessing's burden be lifted...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's the only way to remove it? *sigh* Poor little guy...

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: The other Entreaty should still be in the place of the vow... The merely ordinary cannot obtain it, but I believe that your little one shall make the right choices...

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: A Golden Entreaty is as important as it is dangerous, so you have to take it to the sacred mountain... Only there can it serve its original purpose. Only there can it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Can it what?

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: Only there can it... I can't quite remember what comes next. Despite having all these memories, and things I want to say, nothing seems to come out.

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: Perhaps my nightmares have plagued me for so long that... Or is it the work of the one who claims to command evolution...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That tends to happen once you get older.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We should get some rest first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, fine. Anyway, from what Paimon understands, you mean that we'll need to take two tokens over to the volcano, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Looks like going with {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]} to the volcano is the only way to get to the bottom of this secret.

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: My apologies. You've helped me so much, but I couldn't answer your question... That said, there is, perhaps, one way we could try to get your answer...

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: Please, step into my memories.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Is that your plan?

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: I may have been lost within dreams, but everything that has ever happened in this city has been recorded by my two tainted eyes.

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: Since you could sense Cocouik's power, you should be able to sense my memories, too. Consider this my way of repaying your kindness.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Copan
dialogues.text: I never thought we'd actually make it this far. This must be the Altar of Primal Flame we were looking for. We can get to the Tonatiuh through here...

dialogues.speaker: Copan
dialogues.text: Hah, I always figured this ragtag bunch of adventurers we put together would be wiped out before we even reached the top of the next hill.

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: And we owe all that to our hero, the number-one adventurer in the Flower-Feather Clan, eh?

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: If he hadn't found the blueprints to Ochkanatlan, we'd probably still be wandering lost through some sewer.

dialogues.speaker: Copan
dialogues.text: *sigh* Let's not bring that up again. How was I to know that this cursed place could foil every single positioning skill I ever learned?

dialogues.speaker: Legba
dialogues.text: By the way, where's our young mystic Liriwu gone off to? I didn't see her when I got up this morning.

dialogues.speaker: Legba
dialogues.text: She might've only joined up with us along the way, but she's come this far, and she's become part of the gang. We can't just leave her in the lurch.

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: You don't have to worry about that at all. That kid's just hiding. Y'know, being scared and all.

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: Last night, I happened to spy her sneaking out. I thought, well, we've no idea what could happen next, so it might just be safer to let her hide for the time being.

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: I mean, compared to us fellas, she's just a kid with hardly any experience adventuring, so I found a safe tower in which to set her down.

dialogues.speaker: Titu
dialogues.text: I'm thinking that we should go find her once everything's finished, of course. That is, if we make it back in one piece, haha...

dialogues.speaker: Legba
dialogues.text: Haha, true, true. I mean, that device was built by a tyrant who plunged the whole nation into the Abyss for his selfish desires. Who knows what further traps await us?

dialogues.speaker: Legba
dialogues.text: Plus, that evil dragon is probably lurking in the shadows somewhere, waiting for just the right moment to ambush us... Gotta stay on guard, no matter what.

dialogues.speaker: Legba
dialogues.text: But still, this is all pretty exciting. If the legends about the Jade of Return are true and we can use it to quell the infernal Abyss, then the world can finally take a well-earned rest.

dialogues.speaker: Legba
dialogues.text: *sigh* Ten years back, when disaster came to Teyvat, even the Pyro Archon sacrificed her life for the cause... It would mean so much if we could obtain something that can rid us of this Abyss once and for all.

dialogues.speaker: Copan
dialogues.text: I'm not sure we should hold out too much hope here. If the Python King Och-Kan had something so powerful, how could the city have fallen into this state?

dialogues.speaker: Copan
dialogues.text: Yo, looks like our hero's back.

dialogues.speaker: Copan
dialogues.text: Now, placing the Pyrophosphorite here will summon a guiding spirit to help us navigate.

dialogues.speaker: Copan
dialogues.text: Y'know what? Once this adventure's all over, let's head back to the Flower-Feather Clan and see how that newborn baby girl of yours is doing. We'll paint the town!

dialogues.speaker: Copan
dialogues.text: Her name's Bona, right? Haha, sounds like a mighty cute little kid. Who knows, she might just grow into an even better adventurer than you!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: "And yet, to defeat the threat of evil once and for all was naught but naive fantasy, for everything comes at a price... But the ones to blame are not those who harbor hope, but those who choose to take advantage of others..."

dialogues.speaker: A Somewhat Strange Noise
dialogues.text: Must you still wear that laughable mask when you meet with me, Och-Kan?

dialogues.speaker: A Somewhat Strange Noise
dialogues.text: The time for you to make a choice has come. You have witnessed for yourself the hatred shown towards you by those you consider your people, your brethren.

dialogues.speaker: A Somewhat Strange Noise
dialogues.text: In their eyes, you are no different from any of the evil dragons who ruled over Natlan. Even now, they cry out for a new Pyro Archon to slay you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: They simply have yet to understand...

dialogues.speaker: A Somewhat Strange Noise
dialogues.text: Is that so? If you were to ask me, you are the one whose comprehension fails. Your attempt to create a kingdom for humans alone is but wishful thinking.

dialogues.speaker: A Somewhat Strange Noise
dialogues.text: Whether it be Yohualtecuhtin, or the vishap kindreds — all have been written into the accords and stitched inextricably into the fabric of this land. You should have accepted the world you live in long ago.

dialogues.speaker: A Somewhat Strange Noise
dialogues.text: Moreover, the blood of the Flamelord runs through your veins. You have betrayed Xbalanque's oath to me, and tried to annihilate my people — but instead, you have opened the door to malevolent forces.

dialogues.speaker: A Somewhat Strange Noise
dialogues.text: How ironic, that the human king who yearned to destroy dragonkind is, in truth, the last dragon-heir to the blood of the ancient dragons in this, the land of primal flame! Is it hate that drives you, or fear?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Be silent...

dialogues.speaker: A Somewhat Strange Noise
dialogues.text: Will you not admit it, then, my beloved son?

dialogues.speaker: A Somewhat Strange Noise
dialogues.text: Without the Flamelord's Blessing, how could you have infiltrated the Core of Chu'ulel and stolen the secrets of the dragons?

dialogues.speaker: A Somewhat Strange Noise
dialogues.text: All these years, you have lied to others, and to yourself as well.

dialogues.speaker: A Somewhat Strange Noise
dialogues.text: Truly disappointing. I thought you would be the one to slay the Pyro Dragon, ascending the throne of all Natlan and creating a new epoch for all dragonkind — and, of course, for all humanity...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Humans have no place in the world you envisioned.

dialogues.speaker: A Somewhat Strange Noise
dialogues.text: A matter of interpretation, I say. Obsession with the individual is a human weakness — just like the fruit of your foolish hysteria. A sign of incomplete "evolution."

dialogues.speaker: A Somewhat Strange Noise
dialogues.text: The borders of the world collapse. It begins here, and shall soon spread throughout all Natlan — until Teyvat is wholly plunged into darkness.

dialogues.speaker: A Somewhat Strange Noise
dialogues.text: You have failed, and humanity also. The only way forward is to honor Xbalanque's pact with me: Piece our Golden Entreaties together, and activate Huitzilopochtli.

dialogues.speaker: A Somewhat Strange Noise
dialogues.text: Your people, those humans, might not survive the cataclysm... But after the scouring, a civilization will blossom that surpasses both that of dragons and humans.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Golden Entreaty is no longer here.

dialogues.speaker: A Somewhat Strange Noise
dialogues.text: What? Did you leave it behind on your toy ship, then? Ah, truly do you burn your bridges! Do you mean to doom the rest of the world, too, with these reckless fantasies of yours?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Give up, foolish dragon.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I will not betray the brave humans who are still fighting on...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A world without humans is a world without meaning.

dialogues.speaker: A Somewhat Strange Noise
dialogues.text: You... truly foolish creature! Is all you have done born out of some deluded "hope"?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes. So long as there's life, there's hope.

dialogues.speaker: A Somewhat Strange Noise
dialogues.text: Be that as it may, it is naught but lingering on in agony. This is precisely what I did not understand about humans.

dialogues.speaker: A Somewhat Strange Noise
dialogues.text: Hope saw you defeat the dragons, and equally, it saw you plunge yourselves into a neverending war...

dialogues.speaker: A Somewhat Strange Noise
dialogues.text: Haha, it seems you are human through and through.

dialogues.speaker: A Somewhat Strange Noise
dialogues.text: Fair enough, then. This might be the last time we meet. I cannot predict what fate awaits you, but as part of my experiment, I will return to collect your soul.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Suit yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There are sins I must atone for.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: "To save my people, I sealed my mind into the Core of Chu'ulel and fought alongside them within this city... Yet I never thought that my body and soul would turn against me... That I would come to harm even more people..."

dialogues.speaker: Bona
dialogues.text: Ah, so that's the truth, then. Looks like my suspicions weren't far off.

dialogues.speaker: Bona
dialogues.text: So not only is this NOT the secret Abyss-taming treasure, but based on the inscriptions carved into it, it is hazardous and should not be touched.

dialogues.speaker: Bona
dialogues.text: As the world was plunged into disaster triggered by the subterranean kingdom, so amidst chaos was this legend forged...

dialogues.speaker: Bona
dialogues.text: The Tonatiuh laden with treasure, a Jade of Return that can cleanse filth... It's all a bunch of bunk. All those adventurers who laid down their lives for this, even my old man...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Cheep! Cheep!

dialogues.speaker: Bona
dialogues.text: Hmm? Are you trying to make me feel better?

dialogues.speaker: Bona
dialogues.text: It's okay, Coco, I get you.

dialogues.speaker: Bona
dialogues.text: Even if the legend of some sacred chalice turns out to be false, just setting out on that quest for it makes you a hero.

dialogues.speaker: Bona
dialogues.text: And what's more, it seems we really do have ourselves a monster here!

dialogues.speaker: Bona
dialogues.text: The one behind this, whoever you are... I don't know why you've lured all of us here...

dialogues.speaker: Bona
dialogues.text: But whatever you're on about — it ends here!

dialogues.speaker: Bona
dialogues.text: I might not ever be one of those adventurers whose names shall be etched into the annals of history...

dialogues.speaker: Bona
dialogues.text: But I, Bona, will put an end to this dark passage of history, with Cocouik by my side!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: "In the end, the girl wasn't able to stop everything, nor was I able to save her... But awakened by her hand, I became a seed, and then, many cycles later, I met you..."

dialogues.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
dialogues.text: The nightmares retell a past of blindness and folly.

dialogues.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
dialogues.text: The scorched earth presages a future of bliss and rebirth.

dialogues.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
dialogues.text: Chosen of Dragons, you have arrived at last. I have been expecting you for some time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who are you?

dialogues.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
dialogues.text: It matters not. What matters is that none may now interrupt our conversation.

dialogues.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
dialogues.text: What do you think? Gorgeous art, no? Tell me, what do you see in this mural?

response.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
response.text: What sort of fighting tournament do you speak of...? *ahem* What this painting depicts are the stages of evolution.

response.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
response.text: Evolving out of the primordial elemental creatures into dragons, then evolving step-by-step into humans, until you step onto the stairway to heaven itself... How puerile. How childish.

response.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
response.text: This child thought that the true history of dragons in Teyvat could be wiped clean with such self-deluded fantasies.

response.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
response.text: Evolution... has always been a concept that belongs to dragons, and dragons alone.

response.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
response.text: To attain a stronger body, to gain ever mightier power, we dragons have had to constantly adapt and transform ourselves based on our environment. This is how we survive.

response.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
response.text: However, humans are exactly the opposite. Most of them can barely control elemental forces. The Descender tossed them into Teyvat, giving them the power to change environments to suit themselves.

response.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
response.text: Yet, these same weak humans are the ones who ultimately took over Natlan and the rest of the world...

response.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
response.text: While we once-mighty dragons, creators of high civilization, have now been relegated to wild beasts and livestock. Do you know why that is?

choices.text: Because they have Archons backing them?

response.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
response.text: Hah! Compared to the sky-war I once fought in, these earthly usurpers are nothing. Besides, there are enough of us remaining, even today, to match them and their forces.

response.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
response.text: Instead, this is what I believe — that we dragons are too powerful. We are a race imprisoned by force. The weak worship the strong, sons follow their fathers, peons serve their sovereigns.

response.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
response.text: Races that by nature pursue power are bound by the very power that all too clearly orders their societies.

response.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
response.text: After the Pyro {RUBY#[D]Xiuhcoatl} Dragon's faked death, all that the descendants of the ancients knew was to kowtow before the throne, watching our civilization deteriorate by the day, marching inexorably towards decline.

response.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
response.text: Our race had reached a dead end. But I found new hope for myself within humanity.

response.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
response.text: Curiosity about the unknown, compassion for fellow humans, and the subsequent courage to take on something far more powerful than oneself.

response.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
response.text: Despite being mere tribes in vassalage to the dragons and living in precarious circumstances, I knew that one day they would build a mighty civilization of their own.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Humans really are something...

response.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
response.text: Indeed. I liked humans, but if I wished to understand them, then observation alone was insufficient. I had to go and live among them, and through them, I hoped to save my race.

response.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
response.text: And so I nurtured my beloved son, a dragon mixed with a human soul who was raised among the human tribes. He would slay the decrepit old Pyro Dragon, and ascend to become the new Dragon Sovereign.

response.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
response.text: But I did not count on that man... Xbalanque... And more unexpected still was the betrayal of my own progeny.

response.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
response.text: Human courage leads them to chase illusory hope and also brings forth terrifying uncertainty — just like the Jade of Return...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So the Jade... What is it?

response.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
response.text: Well, if I must, I'd say it's like a beast trap for capturing the lions of Natlan.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Lions? What do you mean by that?

response.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
response.text: Hmm? Well... The noblest of beasts, of course — but that doesn't matter.

response.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
response.text: There are no lions in Natlan, and so, no Jade of Return. Humans always love chasing after things that don't exist, so I created this legend for them.

response.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
response.text: To test these legends, I donned masks and traversed their world in different guises. This isn't the first time that we've met, in fact.

response.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
response.text: Of course, I have my foolish, greedy child to thank for this, who devoured enough souls for me to fashion these masks. Don't you find it all fascinating?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: More like horrendous...

response.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
response.text: Really? I am of the persuasion that experiments are a must. Och-Kan's betrayal taught me that I still have much to learn when it comes to humans, after all.

response.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
response.text: But I fear that this grace has run thin, and darkness will soon engulf this land... Och-Kan bet once and won, but shall we dragons continue betting with humans like this?

response.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
response.text: Be it humans or Yohualtecuhtin, the world will fall into peril again and again because of their inability to resist the dark foe.

response.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
response.text: Chosen of Dragons, hope resides within you. This is not the end. Take the token of the oath, and go unto the sacred mountain.

response.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
response.text: #We shall meet again when all is done. And when that time comes, you shall be the one to decide matters, {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: "This is not the end for you. Take that which is my part, and set off on your journey."

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: "I believe you shall find the answer you seek at the end of your journey."

choices.text: Because the Pyro Dragon is too weak.

response.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
response.text: You think it's because the Pyro Dragon's power has declined, do you?

response.speaker: A Somewhat Strange "Person"
response.text: Ha, this painting depicts the stages of evolution. Evolving out of the primordial elemental creatures and into the dragons, then into humans after a few more steps, until one walks upon the stairway to heaven itself... A puerile notion.

dialogues.text: Finally, after all these years — I have awakened...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?! Who are you? How did you gain the ability to speak?
#What a long journey it has been. {NICKNAME}, Paimon... It is a pleasure to meet you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so you still recognize us! Great! So who are you now, then? Can Paimon still call you Cocouik?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're Och-Kan, then?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Do you mean the Python King — the same one who used to rule all Ochkanatlan?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But didn't Cocouik turn into that? And it still recognizes us — wait, doesn't this mean that this is Cocouik's true...

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: Coco... Yes. That's what that girl called me — the one who woke me up from the Core of Chu'ulel... But I could not save her...

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: Hundreds of years have passed since then... and at last, I've finally found my old body.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Cocouik"...
Cocouik... Yes. Yes. That's what that girl called me — the one who woke me up from the Core of Chu'ulel... But I could not save her...
Hundreds of years have passed since then... and at last, I've finally found my old body.

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: Just call me Och-Kan, please.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Err, are you saying that you're the same Python King who used to rule all Ochkanatlan? But Cocouik turned into you... So all along, it was—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, do you mean that Bona awakened you hundreds of years ago?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That... can't be! We just came on an adventure here with her. She couldn't have been alive for so long, could she?

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: Truly? I could be mistaken... My present memories are as numerous as they are a mess, and I fear I remember things from before far better than my adventures as Cocouik...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Can we still count on you as a comrade, then?

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: Certainly. That is, if you remain willing to accept me... I once split my mind off to protect the people of Ochkanatlan...

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: I never expected my spirit and body to both be swallowed up by the Abyss... To be used by "that person" to commit such an awful litany of crimes...

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: Though my sins cannot be washed away like this Abyssal filth can, this nightmare has finally come to an end — thanks to you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You won't oppose us, will you?

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: Surely not! That is, if you would still accept me... I once split my mind off to protect the people of Ochkanatlan...

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: I never expected my spirit and body to both be swallowed up by the Abyss... To be used by "that person" to commit such an awful litany of crimes...

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: Though my sins cannot be washed away like this Abyssal filth can, this nightmare has finally come to an end — thanks to you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Who's this "person" you're mentioning? Bona mentioned that earlier while we were on the Tonatiuh too. Is there someone pulling the strings behind the scenes whom we don't know about?

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: Heh. Since you're here, you must've already met "that person." You do possess this Golden Entreaty, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right. In fact, we only got here because that wicked dragon stole our Golden Entreaty... Hang on, guess we shouldn't call it "wicked" from now on, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I doubt it cares what you call it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, out with it, wicked dragon. Why'd you steal our token?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? Seriously, you're so rude!

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: That Golden Entreaty... is very important.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Sure is. Based on what Manqu told us before, it can help cure {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}, but Bona said that it holds the key to quelling the Abyss.

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: The child is right: It can indeed tame the filth of the Abyss for all of Natlan... But not in the way that you imagine... Which is why I had to hide it on the ship...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What do you mean? That sounds kinda dangerous. Definitely not the sort of thing you'd use willy-nilly... Err, what should we do next, then?

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: Hmm. And another thing. Your companion there, that little Tepetlisaurus...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #You mean {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}?

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: #Yes. {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}... is most similar to me...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What do you mean? You look very different...

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: Our bloodlines both contain the Flamelord's Blessing...

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: So I believe that your friend will make the right choice... A Golden Entreaty is dangerous and important in equal measure, so you must go with it to the sacred mountain... And then, with it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "And then, with it" what?

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: And then... Hmm. I cannot quite remember what comes next. Despite having all these memories, and many things I wish to say, nothing comes hither to my lips.

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: Is this because I've been plagued by nightmares for so long...? No. "That person" must be stirring the pot again.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That tends to happen once you get older.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We should get some rest first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, fine. Anyway, from what Paimon understands, you mean that we'll need to take these two tokens over to the volcano, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Looks like we've gotta get {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]} to the volcano if we wanna get to the bottom of all this.

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: My apologies. You've helped me so much, but I couldn't answer your question... That said, there is, perhaps, one way we could try to get your answer...

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: Please, step into my memories.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Is that your plan?

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: I may have been lost within dreams, but everything that has ever happened in this city has been recorded by my two tainted eyes.

dialogues.speaker: Och-Kan
dialogues.text: Since you could sense Cocouik's power, you should be able to sense my memories, too. Consider this my way of repaying your kindness.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you.

talks.objective: Look for answers within Och-Kan's memories
Look for answers within Och-Kan's memories
Look for answers within Och-Kan's memories

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh... You're finally back.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, you've returned from that memory, so why is Coco... Och-Kan, still not moving...?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's very tired. It's going to need a good long rest.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, you do get tired easily when you grow old. Well, at least it can have a good rest now...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Right?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yep.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #What did you see in the memory just now, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You recount what you witnessed within Och-Kan's mind to Paimon in the simplest way you can...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Huh!? You saw {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}, and there was some weird guy with him on the Tonatiuh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Uh oh. That might not be a memory, but something that's happening right now! {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]} might be in danger...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You claim he just said a bunch of weird things, but Paimon's still somewhat worried. Let's hurry back to the Tonatiuh and check things out.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But before that...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh yeah, the Golden Entreaty...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Based on what Och-Kan said, it has incredible uses, but it's also very dangerous and shouldn't be used lightly... We're going to have to tell Bona that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #But then, we can't give it to her either, can we? We'll have to take it to the volcano with {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}... Though we don't know what to do with it once we get there...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: About Bona...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh yeah, you saw her in the memory as well. Guess Och-Kan's right — she really is from hundreds of years ago, then?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But how did she live for so long? It's like she's adventuring with us for the first time, and it doesn't feel like she's trying to deceive us either. Could it be that she's actually...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's head back to the Tonatiuh first. We can talk about this then.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright. We managed to find the Tonatiuh, so Bona and her father's adventures won't be considered crazy or groundless stories any longer.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Plus, we also got this Jade of Return... Whatever it may be, Paimon's sure it's important somehow.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, all in all, this adventure has been pretty meaningful!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hey! Don't try to take on {REALNAME[ID(2)|SHOWHOST(true)]}'s role just because he's not around!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe. In that case, let's head back to the Tonatiuh when you're ready.
